- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
tools.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
tools.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
tools.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
tools.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
tools.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index
tools.description:
Fetches URL content, converts HTML to markdown (JSON is chunked by key paths, plain text indexed directly), persists it in a searchable knowledge base, and returns a small preview window per source. The raw page bytes never enter your conversation — they live in storage and you retrieve any section on-demand via ctx_search.

Caching: every fetch is cached on disk and reused for repeat calls within the TTL window. The default TTL is 24 hours; override per-call with the `ttl` parameter (milliseconds, `ttl: 0` bypasses cache like `force: true`). Stored content older than 14 days is cleaned up on startup.

WHEN:
  - You need web content (docs, changelogs, API references, spec pages) and the raw page bytes should NOT enter your conversation
  - Multi-URL research (library evaluation, migration scans, doc comparisons): pass the `requests` array and a `concurrency` value 2-8 for parallel I/O
  - You want repeat lookups against the same URL to be cheap (TTL cache hits return only a hint, no re-fetch)
  - You want a long-lived cache window (override `ttl` upward for stable specs) or a guaranteed-fresh fetch (`ttl: 0` or `force: true`)

WHEN NOT:
  - You already have the content locally — store it via the inline index tool
  - The page is SPA-rendered (JavaScript-required to materialize content) — this is a plain HTTP fetch, no headless browser

RETURNS:
  Per-source preview windows extracted around indexable headings plus indexing metadata (chunk counts, source labels, cache state). Raw content is NOT echoed back — retrieve any section on-demand via ctx_search(source: "<label>"). Concurrency parallelizes the fetch phase up to your chosen value (capped by the host's logical CPU count); the FTS5 write phase always runs serially because SQLite is a single-writer store. Net latency = max(fetch latency across the pool) + sum(per-source index write time). Cache hits skip both phases and return a small freshness hint instead of re-fetching. Use 4-8 for stable I/O-bound batches; lower the value when the target host enforces a per-IP rate limit you cannot raise.

EXAMPLE: ctx_fetch_and_index(
  requests: [{url: "https://react.dev/...", source: "react"}, {url: "https://vuejs.org/...", source: "vue"}],
  concurrency: 5
)

url.description: Single URL to fetch and index (legacy single-shape)

source.description: Label for the indexed content when using single `url` (e.g., 'React useEffect docs', 'Supabase Auth API'). For batch, put source in each requests entry.
Label for this URL's indexed content

requests.description: Batch shape: array of {url, source?} entries. Use with concurrency>1 for parallel fetch. Each request indexed under its own source label. Output preserves input order.

concurrency.description: Max URLs to fetch in parallel (1-8, default: 1). Use 4-8 for I/O-bound multi-URL batches (library docs, changelogs, pricing pages). Capped by os.cpus().length on small machines (response notes when capped). Indexing is always serial regardless — only fetches race.

force.description: Skip cache and re-fetch even if content was recently indexed

ttl.description: Override the cache freshness window for this call, in milliseconds. `ttl: 0` bypasses the cache like `force: true`; omit to use the default 24h TTL.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search
tools.description:
Search a unified knowledge base with a multi-strategy ranking pipeline. Two parallel matchers run on every query: a Porter-stemming matcher ("caching" finds "cached", "caches", "cach") and a trigram-substring matcher ("useEff" finds "useEffect"). Their ranked lists are merged via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, so a document that ranks well in both surfaces above one that wins only on a single strategy. Multi-term queries get an additional proximity-rerank pass that boosts passages where the query terms appear close together. Typos are corrected via Levenshtein distance and re-searched. Result snippets are window-extracted around the matched terms, not blindly truncated.

The knowledge base is unified: queries reach indexed content you stored (ctx_index, ctx_fetch_and_index, ctx_batch_execute output) AND auto-captured session memory written by hooks (decisions, errors, blockers, plans, user prompts, rejected approaches, tool failures, compaction guides — 26 event categories). File-backed sources carry a content hash and auto-flag staleness when the source file changes.

WHEN:
  - You want to recall something that exists in storage (recently indexed content, prior session events, auto-memory) instead of re-reading raw sources
  - You have multiple related questions about the same body of knowledge — batch every question into one call (the ranking pipeline runs per-query but the round-trip cost is paid once)
  - You want to scope the query to one labelled source (pass `source` — partial match is fine)
  - You want a chronological view across current session + prior sessions + persistent auto-memory (pass `sort: "timeline"` — the default `relevance` mode only ranks within the current session)
  - You want to filter ranked results by content shape (pass `contentType: "code"` to surface implementation snippets or `contentType: "prose"` to surface explanations)

WHEN NOT:
  - The data you want to query has never been stored in the knowledge base AND no session memory has accumulated around it — capture first (run a gather-and-index call), then come back here to query
  - You have one ad-hoc question against data that is not in the knowledge base — answer it inline by running code in the sandbox tool; one round-trip instead of capture-then-query

RETURNS:
  Per-query ranked sections with window-extracted snippets. Use 2-4 specific technical terms per query. Common session-memory source labels: `decision` (user corrections / preferences), `error` and `error-resolution` (past failures + their fixes), `blocker`, `plan`, `user-prompt`, `rejected-approach`, `compaction` (post-compact session guide). See ctx_stats for live category counts. Each response carries a throttle counter (call #N/M in the rolling time window); results taper toward the soft cap and calls block after the hard cap. Tune via CONTEXT_MODE_SEARCH_WINDOW_MS, CONTEXT_MODE_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_AFTER, CONTEXT_MODE_SEARCH_BLOCK_AFTER.

EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["root cause", "proposed fix", "test coverage"], source: "issue-#683")
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["what did we decide about caching"], source: "decision", sort: "timeline")
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["useEffect cleanup pattern"], source: "react-docs", contentType: "code", limit: 5)
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["last user prompt", "active skills", "open blockers"], sort: "timeline")

queries.description: Array of search queries. Batch ALL questions in one call.

source.description: Filter to a specific indexed source (partial match).

contentType.description: Filter results by content type: 'code' or 'prose'.

sort.description: Sort mode. 'relevance' (default): BM25 ranked, current session only. 'timeline': chronological across current session, prior sessions, and auto-memory.

project.description: Project scope. Default (omit): this session's project — auto-resolved from the host adapter. 'global': span every project in the shared store (cross-project recall). <absolute-path>: scope to that specific project directory.

content.content: Launching skill: claude-in-chrome

content.text:
# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp

content.text:
I've pinned it down, and the fix is designed. I haven't applied it yet.

**Cause:** the dropdown hover is `--dd-hover-bg: violet` with `--dd-hover-color: fg-0`. I reproduced it live: `#adbcbc` text on `#af88eb` in dark. That's **1.30:1 in light and 1.42:1 in dark**, where readable text needs 4.5. The pairing comes straight from the reference. In Catppuccin the text colour happened to contrast with the mauve, and my mapping lost that.

**Fix:** a lilac tint for the hover background and `fg-1` for the text.
- Background: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--violet) 30%, var(--bg-0))`.
- Text: `var(--fg-1)`.
- Contrast: 5.55:1 in light and 5.25:1 in dark.

It stays clearly purple but no longer solid. I'll add a test that resolves the pair per variant and fails below 4.5, watch it fail first, and then make the fix.

**Timing:** the fresh reviewer is still reading the branch. Editing underneath it would give it a red test suite to report. So I'll apply the fix as soon as it finishes, together with anything it finds, and re-paste into Kagi afterwards.

**Wider audit:** I checked every background and text pair the theme declares. The worst are these:

| Pair | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dropdown hover (your report) | 1.30 | 1.42 |
| Result-summary highlight | 2.52 | 2.35 |
| Assistant bubble and `kagi-accent` backgrounds with `fg-0` | 3.11 | 3.00 |
| Filled buttons, checkbox, beta tag and sidebar hover in light | 2.98–4.13 | fine |

Two other points:
- Accent text in light (links, URLs) sits at about 3.1–3.6:1 on cream. That comes from Selenized's own accent values, so I'd leave it.
- A few rows may not match how Kagi actually uses those variables, so treat the table as pointers.

Do you want me to fix the result-summary highlight and filled-button pairs in the same pass, or only the dropdown?

    p["grey-2"] = mix(p["bg-2"], p["dim"], 2 / 3)
    p["grey-3"] = mix(p["dim"], p["fg-0"], 1 / 3)

        )
        out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out)

    dst.write_text(convert(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), encoding="utf-8")

        c / 255 / 12.92 if c / 255 <= 0.04045 else ((c / 255 + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4

    )
    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b

content.text: <total_tokens>14956456 tokens left</total_tokens>

Rod, the dropdown hover is fixed and live, but my first attempt didn't work and I only caught that by re-testing in the browser. Your Kagi account has the fixed CSS. The file is `/Users/rod/x/kagi-selenized/kagi-selenized.css` and the branch is `feature/selenized-theme`.

**The dropdown fix**
- **What went wrong first:** I overrode `--dd-hover-bg` and `--dd-hover-color`. Those aren't what Kagi's filter dropdown reads, and the live style didn't change after I saved. The tests passed anyway, because they checked my diagnosis and not the page. That first commit stays in the history.
- **The real cause:** Kagi's rule `.filter-item.dropdown:…:is(:focus-within, :hover)` uses `--primary-100` (violet) as the background and `--primary` (`fg-0` grey) as the text. That's 1.3:1 in light and 1.4:1 in dark.
- **The fix:** an appended rule with the same selector gives a violet tint (`color-mix(violet 30%, bg-0)`) with `fg-1` text. That's 5.55:1 in light and 5.25:1 in dark.
- **Checked in the browser:** in dark, the hovered pill is now `#405379` with `#cad8d9` text. I couldn't flip your OS to light, so light is checked by calculation only.

**Reviewer verdict:** no Critical findings, and the file regenerates byte-identical from the gist. It said "ready to merge with fixes". The one Important finding needs your decision.

**Your decision: grey surfaces with `fg-0` text**

| Surface | Light | Dark | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg-2` | 3.75 | 3.80 | domain chips, date chips |
| `grey-1` | 3.11 | 3.00 | assistant answer bubble, active thread |
| `grey-2` | 2.52 | 2.35 | result-summary highlight, dropdown rows |

In Catppuccin all of those were background shades. In Selenized, `bg-2` is already the selection colour, and `dim` is a text colour. So anything mixed between them is a mid-tone that's poor as either. The options:
1. Make body text `fg-1`. That gives 5.6–8 on every surface, but text becomes darker than Selenized intends.
2. Pull the greys towards `bg-1` and `bg-2`. That gives roughly 4.2–4.4 and flatter hover states.
3. Accept it as Selenized's own trade-off and say so in the spec.

I'd go with 1, but it changes the look everywhere, so it's your call.

**Rulings I made**
1. The `color-mix` rewrite of `rgba(30, 30, 46, 0)`. It costs nothing visible if wrong.
2. The black and white `rgba` shadows are left as they are.
3. Generation uses `python build_theme.py SRC DST`. The reviewer showed `-I` works in that form, so I've corrected my earlier rationale.
4. The "no old names left" test only covers names that change.
5. The real-reference test checks "no new unresolved `var()`", because two names are unresolved in the gist itself. If a new typo happened to match one of those two, it would slip through.
6. I replaced your Solarized custom CSS. A backup is at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rod-x/d6df8a6a-bd60-4933-93b0-b66ba0500269/scratchpad/kagi-custom-css-backup-solarized.css`, and re-pasting it undoes everything.
7. The wrong first dropdown fix, described above.

**Deferred minors** (none acted on)
- Primary button text on violet in light is 3.58:1, and no in-palette colour reaches 4.5.
- `convert()` has some robustness gaps. Split palette runs emit twice, a palette line with a trailing comment keeps its old name, and any selector other than `:root` is treated as dark.
- Without the cloned gist, the strongest test skips.
- Dark red (3.71), bright red (4.15) and violet (4.28) are inherent to Selenized.
- Light-mode cyan links are 3.08:1. Selenized `blue` (4.35) or `br-blue` (4.64) would be more legible, at some cost in fidelity to the gist.
- `--dd-list-input-bg` is declared twice, inherited from the gist.
- `fg-1`, `grey-3` and most `br-*` colours are defined but unused.

**Other notes**
- The Assistant (`assistant.kagi.com`) stays in Kagi's default styling, because custom CSS doesn't apply on that origin.
- My earlier audit table was only a set of pointers. I haven't verified that Kagi uses each variable the way I assumed, as the dropdown showed.

Which option do you want for the grey surfaces? After that I can finish the branch: merge it, open a PR, or leave it as it is. I'm leaving the working notes in place until you decide.

NAME_MAP = {
    "base": "bg-0",
    "mantle": "bg-1",
    "crust": "bg-1",
    "surface0": "bg-2",
    "surface1": "grey-1",
    "surface2": "grey-2",

    "yellow": "yellow",

}


def _channels(color: str) -> list[int]:
    return [int(color[i : i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]


def mix(a: str, b: str, t: float) -> str:
    mixed = (int(x + (y - x) * t + 0.5) for x, y in zip(_channels(a), _channels(b)))
    return "#" + "".join(f"{c:02x}" for c in mixed)


def _luminance(color: str) -> float:
    r, g, b = (
        c / 255 / 12.92 if c / 255 <= 0.04045 else ((c / 255 + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
        for c in _channels(color)
    )
    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b


def contrast(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    hi, lo = sorted((_luminance(a), _luminance(b)), reverse=True)
    return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05)


def _palette(values: Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    p: dict[str, str] = dict(zip(NAMES, values))
    p["grey-1"] = mix(p["bg-2"], p["dim"], 1 / 3)
    p["grey-2"] = mix(p["bg-2"], p["dim"], 2 / 3)
    p["grey-3"] = mix(p["dim"], p["fg-0"], 1 / 3)
    p["grey-4"] = mix(p["dim"], p["fg-0"], 2 / 3)
    return p


PALETTES = {"light": _palette(_LIGHT), "dark": _palette(_DARK)}


APPENDED_RULES = """

.filter-item.dropdown:not(.filter_item_icon, .filter_item_single):is(:focus-within, :hover) {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--violet) 30%, var(--bg-0));
  color: var(--fg-1);
}
"""

_PALETTE_DECL = re.compile(
    r"^(\s*)--(?:" + "|".join(NAME_MAP) + r"):\s*#[0-9a-fA-F]{6};\s*$"
)
_RULE_OPEN = re.compile(r"^\s*([^{}]*?)\s*\{\s*$")
_DECL = re.compile(r"^\s*--([\w-]+)\s*:")
_OLD_REF = re.compile(r"var\(--(" + "|".join(NAME_MAP) + r")(?=[,)])")
_BASE_ALPHA = re.compile(r"rgba\(30, 30, 46, ([\d.]+)\)")


def _variant(selector: str) -> str:
    return "light" if selector == ":root" else "dark"


def convert(css: str) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []
    selector = ""
    in_palette_run = False
    for line in css.split("\n"):
        if match := _RULE_OPEN.match(line):
            selector = match.group(1)
        palette_line = _PALETTE_DECL.match(line)
        if palette_line:
            if not in_palette_run:
                indent = palette_line.group(1)
                out.extend(
                    f"{indent}--{name}: {value};"
                    for name, value in PALETTES[_variant(selector)].items()
                )
            in_palette_run = True
            continue
        in_palette_run = False
        if (decl := _DECL.match(line)) and decl.group(1) in PALETTES["light"]:
            raise ValueError(f"--{decl.group(1)} is already declared in the source")
        line = _OLD_REF.sub(lambda m: f"var(--{NAME_MAP[m.group(1)]}", line)
        line = _BASE_ALPHA.sub(
            lambda m: (
                f"color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg-0) {float(m.group(1)) * 100:g}%, transparent)"
            ),
            line,
        )
        out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out) + APPENDED_RULES


def main(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    dst.write_text(convert(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    main(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))

Rod, the enabled toggles are fixed and live in your Kagi account, and I've checked both light and dark. The branch is `feature/selenized-theme` at `6757887`.

**Cause:** Kagi colours a checked toggle's bar with `--purple-600` and its knob with `--white`. In this theme those came out as teal and the body-text grey.

| Mode | Teal bar vs panel | Grey knob vs bar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Light | 2.67:1 (below the 3:1 UI minimum) | 1.74:1 |
| Dark | fine | 1.06:1, so the knob effectively vanished |

**Fix:** two appended rules. The bar and its border are `br-green`, which matches the green border the "off" state already has. The knob is `bg-0`. Contrast against the panel is 3.34:1 or better in both modes, and the knob against the bar is 3.85:1 or better.

**Checked live** using the Control Centre theme selector:

| Mode | Bar | Knob |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Light | `rgb(66, 139, 0)` | `rgb(251, 243, 219)` |
| Dark | `rgb(132, 199, 71)` | `rgb(16, 60, 72)` |

The toggle in the filter row (next to "Fediverse Forums") uses the same rules. I checked "Enable Custom CSS" and the other enabled toggles in the panel, but I didn't switch the Fediverse toggle on, since that would change your search filters.

**Your theme setting:** it showed **Light** when I started, so I set it back to Light after testing dark.

**Tests and process:** 25 tests pass, including new ones for the toggle contrast against both page backgrounds in both variants. This time I measured the real cause in the browser first, then wrote the failing test, applied the fix, and verified live before committing.

**One scope note:** the reference also has older rules for a `.--enabled` toggle markup. I left those alone because I didn't see them in use on the pages I checked. If you spot a toggle that still looks off, tell me where and I'll check it.

**Still open:**
- The grey-surface contrast question from before (domain chips, answer bubble, summary highlight at 2.4–3.8:1 with `fg-0` text). My recommendation is to make body text `fg-1`, but it changes the look everywhere.
- What to do with the branch when you're done. I'm leaving my working notes in place until then.

import re
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

NAMES = [
    "bg-0",
    "bg-1",
    "bg-2",
    "dim",

NAME_MAP = {
    "base": "bg-0",
    "mantle": "bg-1",
    "crust": "bg-1",
    "surface0": "bg-2",
    "surface1": "grey-1",
    "surface2": "grey-2",
    "overlay0": "dim",
    "overlay1": "grey-3",
    "subtext0": "grey-3",

    "maroon": "br-red",
    "red": "red",
    "green": "green",
    "yellow": "yellow",
    "blue": "blue",
}


def _channels(color: str) -> list[int]:
    return [int(color[i : i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]


def mix(a: str, b: str, t: float) -> str:
    mixed = (int(x + (y - x) * t + 0.5) for x, y in zip(_channels(a), _channels(b)))
    return "#" + "".join(f"{c:02x}" for c in mixed)


def _luminance(color: str) -> float:
    r, g, b = (
        c / 255 / 12.92 if c / 255 <= 0.04045 else ((c / 255 + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
        for c in _channels(color)
    )
    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b


def contrast(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    hi, lo = sorted((_luminance(a), _luminance(b)), reverse=True)
    return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05)


def _palette(values: Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    p: dict[str, str] = dict(zip(NAMES, values))
    p["grey-1"] = mix(p["bg-2"], p["dim"], 1 / 3)
    p["grey-2"] = mix(p["bg-2"], p["dim"], 2 / 3)
    p["grey-3"] = mix(p["dim"], p["fg-0"], 1 / 3)
    p["grey-4"] = mix(p["dim"], p["fg-0"], 2 / 3)
    return p


PALETTES = {"light": _palette(_LIGHT), "dark": _palette(_DARK)}


APPENDED_RULES = """

.filter-item.dropdown:not(.filter_item_icon, .filter_item_single):is(:focus-within, :hover) {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--violet) 30%, var(--bg-0));
  color: var(--fg-1);
}

.k_ui_toggle_switch input:checked ~ .k_ui_toggle_switch_bar {
  background: var(--br-green);
  border-color: var(--br-green);
}

.k_ui_toggle_switch input:checked ~ .k_ui_toggle_switch_bar::after {
  background-color: var(--bg-0);
}
"""

_PALETTE_DECL = re.compile(
    r"^(\s*)--(?:" + "|".join(NAME_MAP) + r"):\s*#[0-9a-fA-F]{6};\s*$"
)
_RULE_OPEN = re.compile(r"^\s*([^{}]*?)\s*\{\s*$")
_DECL = re.compile(r"^\s*--([\w-]+)\s*:")
_OLD_REF = re.compile(r"var\(--(" + "|".join(NAME_MAP) + r")(?=[,)])")
_BASE_ALPHA = re.compile(r"rgba\(30, 30, 46, ([\d.]+)\)")


def _variant(selector: str) -> str:
    return "light" if selector == ":root" else "dark"


def convert(css: str) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []
    selector = ""
    in_palette_run = False
    for line in css.split("\n"):
        if match := _RULE_OPEN.match(line):
            selector = match.group(1)
        palette_line = _PALETTE_DECL.match(line)
        if palette_line:
            if not in_palette_run:
                indent = palette_line.group(1)
                out.extend(
                    f"{indent}--{name}: {value};"
                    for name, value in PALETTES[_variant(selector)].items()
                )
            in_palette_run = True
            continue
        in_palette_run = False
        if (decl := _DECL.match(line)) and decl.group(1) in PALETTES["light"]:
            raise ValueError(f"--{decl.group(1)} is already declared in the source")
        line = _OLD_REF.sub(lambda m: f"var(--{NAME_MAP[m.group(1)]}", line)
        line = _BASE_ALPHA.sub(
            lambda m: (
                f"color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg-0) {float(m.group(1)) * 100:g}%, transparent)"
            ),
            line,
        )
        out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out) + APPENDED_RULES


def main(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    dst.write_text(convert(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    main(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))

def _channels(color: str) -> list[int]:
    return [int(color[i : i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]


def mix(a: str, b: str, t: float) -> str:
    mixed = (int(x + (y - x) * t + 0.5) for x, y in zip(_channels(a), _channels(b)))

_DECL = re.compile(r"^\s*--([\w-]+)\s*:")
_OLD_REF = re.compile(r"var\(--(" + "|".join(NAME_MAP) + r")(?=[,)])")
_BASE_ALPHA = re.compile(r"rgba\(30, 30, 46, ([\d.]+)\)")


def _variant(selector: str) -> str:
    return "light" if selector == ":root" else "dark"


def convert(css: str) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []

                out.extend(
                    f"{indent}--{name}: {value};"

**Domain popup**

| Part | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ranking bar | Kagi gave it a magenta background and cyan labels. | `bg-2` background, `fg-1` labels. |

It's how Selenized's own red pairs with its background, and no palette colour does better. I gave that one test its own 4.0 threshold and recorded it as a ruling. Say if you'd rather Block use the plain dark pill.

- The info note in states other than Default. I didn't want to change your domain preference to see them.
- Other Kagi panels that use the same magenta bar colour or the same undefined note variable. If another one looks off, tell me which and I'll check it.

# Kagi Selenized

A [Selenized](https://github.com/jan-warchol/selenized) theme for
[Kagi](https://kagi.com) search, as a custom CSS file. It follows your
system setting: Selenized Light in light mode, Selenized Dark in dark mode.

This is an unofficial theme and is not affiliated with Kagi.

## Screenshots

Selenized Light:

![Kagi search for capybara in Selenized Light](docs/screenshots/capybara-light.png)

Selenized Dark:

![Kagi search for capybara in Selenized Dark](docs/screenshots/capybara-dark.png)

## Install

1. Copy the contents of [`kagi-selenized.css`](kagi-selenized.css).
1. In Kagi, open **Settings**, then **Appearance**, then **Custom CSS**, and
   choose **Change**.
1. Paste the CSS, then choose **Save Changes**.
1. Make sure **Enable Custom CSS** is on. It is in the Control Centre
   (the top-right icon on the search page).

Your existing custom CSS is replaced when you paste, so keep a copy of it
first. Kagi offers `?no_css` on a search URL if you ever need to switch the
CSS off temporarily.

## What it covers

- Search results, filters, header, side panels and the Control Centre.
- Both Selenized variants, using the canonical sRGB values.

Not covered:

- Kagi's settings pages. Kagi does not apply custom CSS there.
- Kagi Assistant. It lives on `assistant.kagi.com`, where custom CSS does
  not apply.
- Kagi can change its markup at any time, which may break individual rules.

## Colour choices

Selenized has fewer neutrals than Catppuccin, so a few choices are worth
knowing about:

- Body text uses `fg-1`, not `fg-0`. `fg-0` is only 3.0 to 3.8:1 on the
  `bg-2` surfaces that Kagi uses for chips and bubbles. `fg-1` gives 5.1:1
  or better on `bg-0`, `bg-1` and `bg-2` in both variants.
- Four greys are interpolated between `bg-2`, `dim` and `fg-0`, to stand in
  for Catppuccin's surface and overlay shades.
- In dark mode, `bg-0` is already the darkest shade, so panels and the header
  sit one step lighter than the page instead of darker.
- Light-mode accent text, such as links, is about 3.1 to 3.6:1 on the page
  background. That comes from Selenized's accent values, which this theme
  does not alter.

A handful of Kagi's own rules produced unreadable text with this palette,
so the file ends with overrides for:

- the filter dropdown hover,
- enabled toggle switches,
- the domain preference popup (ranking bar, buttons and note).

Each is checked by a contrast test and was verified in Kagi in both modes.

## How it is built

The CSS is generated, not hand-written. `build_theme.py` takes a Catppuccin
Kagi theme and rewrites it for Selenized:

- It replaces the palette block in each scope (light `:root`, and the two
  dark scopes) with Selenized values.
- It renames every `var(--old)` reference using a mapping table, and fails
  if a new name would collide with one already declared.
- It appends the overrides above and the licence header.

The input is a gist by jcrabapple:
<https://repo.jcrabapple.com/jcrabapple/82208449e52b434a8e695c8124fa3f79>,
at revision `1ae117e4a5bc74ff7bbbf3496eef80e4dffe312b`. The output is
byte-identical when regenerated from that revision.

To regenerate and test (needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and
Python 3.13 or later):

```bash
git clone https://repo.jcrabapple.com/jcrabapple/82208449e52b434a8e695c8124fa3f79.git reference/gist
uv run python build_theme.py reference/gist/kagi-catppuccin-mocha.css kagi-selenized.css
uv run pytest
```

`reference/` is git-ignored. Without it, the test that runs against the real
gist is skipped.

## Credits

- [Selenized](https://github.com/jan-warchol/selenized) by Jan Warchoł.
- The Catppuccin theme this was converted from, by jcrabapple (linked above).
  The gist does not state a licence that I could find, so check with its
  author before redistributing anything derived from it.

## Licence

[MIT No Attribution](LICENSE). The same text is at the top of the CSS file.

# Kagi Selenized

A [Selenized](https://github.com/jan-warchol/selenized) theme for
[Kagi](https://kagi.com) search, as a custom CSS file. It follows your
system setting: Selenized Light in light mode, Selenized Dark in dark mode.

This is an unofficial theme and is not affiliated with Kagi.

## Screenshots

Selenized Light:

![Capybara search, Selenized Light](docs/screenshots/capybara-light.png)

Selenized Dark:

![Capybara search, Selenized Dark](docs/screenshots/capybara-dark.png)

## Install

1. Copy the contents of [`kagi-selenized.css`](kagi-selenized.css).
1. In Kagi, open **Settings**, then **Appearance**, then **Custom CSS**, and
   choose **Change**.
1. Paste the CSS, then choose **Save Changes**.
1. Make sure **Enable Custom CSS** is on. It is in the Control Centre
   (the top-right icon on the search page).

Your existing custom CSS is replaced when you paste, so keep a copy of it
first. Kagi offers `?no_css` on a search URL if you ever need to switch the
CSS off temporarily.

## What it covers

- Search results, filters, header, side panels and the Control Centre.
- Both Selenized variants, using the canonical sRGB values.

Not covered:

- Kagi's settings pages. Kagi does not apply custom CSS there.
- Kagi Assistant. It lives on `assistant.kagi.com`, where custom CSS does
  not apply.
- Kagi can change its markup at any time, which may break individual rules.

## Colour choices

Selenized has fewer neutrals than Catppuccin, so a few choices are worth
knowing about:

- Body text uses `fg-1`, not `fg-0`. `fg-0` is only 3.8:1 on the `bg-2`
  surfaces that Kagi uses for chips and bubbles. `fg-1` gives 5.1:1 or
  better on `bg-0`, `bg-1` and `bg-2` in both variants. Text on the
  interpolated greys is lower still (`fg-1` on `grey-1` is 4.0:1 in dark).
- Four greys are interpolated between `bg-2`, `dim` and `fg-0`, to stand in
  for Catppuccin's surface and overlay shades.
- In dark mode, `bg-0` is already the darkest shade, so panels and the header
  sit one step lighter than the page instead of darker.
- Light-mode accent text, such as links, is about 3.1 to 3.6:1 on the page
  background. That comes from Selenized's accent values, which this theme
  does not alter.

A handful of Kagi's own rules produced unreadable text with this palette,
so the file ends with overrides for:

- the filter dropdown hover,
- enabled toggle switches,
- the domain preference popup (ranking bar, buttons and note).

Each is covered by a contrast test. The toggles and the popup were checked
in Kagi in both modes; the dropdown hover was only checked live in dark.

## How it is built

The CSS is generated, not hand-written. `build_theme.py` takes a Catppuccin
Kagi theme and rewrites it for Selenized:

- It replaces the palette block in each scope (light `:root`, and the two
  dark scopes) with Selenized values.
- It renames every `var(--old)` reference using a mapping table, and fails
  if a new name would collide with one already declared.
- It appends the overrides above and the licence header.

The input is a gist by jcrabapple:
<https://repo.jcrabapple.com/jcrabapple/82208449e52b434a8e695c8124fa3f79>,
at revision `1ae117e4a5bc74ff7bbbf3496eef80e4dffe312b`. The output is
byte-identical when regenerated from that revision.

To regenerate and test (needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and
Python 3.13 or later):

```bash
git clone \
  https://repo.jcrabapple.com/jcrabapple/82208449e52b434a8e695c8124fa3f79.git \
  reference/gist
uv run python build_theme.py \
  reference/gist/kagi-catppuccin-mocha.css kagi-selenized.css
uv run pytest
```

`reference/` is git-ignored. Without it, the test that runs against the real
gist is skipped.

## Credits

- [Selenized](https://github.com/jan-warchol/selenized) by Jan Warchoł.
- The Catppuccin theme this was converted from, by jcrabapple (linked above).
  The gist does not state a licence that I could find, so check with its
  author before redistributing anything derived from it.

## Licence

# Kagi Selenized

A [Selenized](https://github.com/jan-warchol/selenized) theme for
[Kagi](https://kagi.com) search, as a custom CSS file. It follows your
system setting: Selenized Light in light mode, Selenized Dark in dark mode.

This is an unofficial theme and is not affiliated with Kagi.

## Screenshots

Selenized Light:

![Capybara search, Selenized Light](docs/screenshots/capybara-light.png)

Selenized Dark:

![Capybara search, Selenized Dark](docs/screenshots/capybara-dark.png)

## Install

1. Copy the contents of [`kagi-selenized.css`](kagi-selenized.css).
1. In Kagi, open **Settings**, then **Appearance**, then **Custom CSS**, and
   choose **Change**.
1. Paste the CSS, then choose **Save Changes**.
1. Make sure **Enable Custom CSS** is on. It is in the Control Centre
   (the top-right icon on the search page).

Your existing custom CSS is replaced when you paste, so keep a copy of it
first. Kagi offers `?no_css` on a search URL if you ever need to switch the
CSS off temporarily.

## What it covers

- Search results, filters, header, side panels and the Control Centre.
- Both Selenized variants, using the canonical sRGB values.

Not covered:

- Kagi's settings pages. Kagi does not apply custom CSS there.
- Kagi Assistant. It lives on `assistant.kagi.com`, where custom CSS does
  not apply.
- Kagi can change its markup at any time, which may break individual rules.

## Colour choices

Selenized has fewer neutrals than Catppuccin, so a few choices are worth
knowing about:

- Body text uses `fg-1`, not `fg-0`. `fg-0` is only 3.8:1 on the `bg-2`
  surfaces that Kagi uses for chips and bubbles. `fg-1` gives 5.1:1 or
  better on `bg-0`, `bg-1` and `bg-2` in both variants. Text on the
  interpolated greys is lower still (`fg-1` on `grey-1` is 4.0:1 in dark).
- Four greys are interpolated between `bg-2`, `dim` and `fg-0`, to stand in
  for Catppuccin's surface and overlay shades.
- In dark mode, `bg-0` is already the darkest shade, so panels and the header
  sit one step lighter than the page instead of darker.
- Light-mode accent text, such as links, is about 3.1 to 3.6:1 on the page
  background. That comes from Selenized's accent values, which this theme
  does not alter.

A handful of Kagi's own rules produced unreadable text with this palette,
so the file ends with overrides for:

- the filter dropdown hover,
- enabled toggle switches,
- the domain preference popup (ranking bar, buttons and note).

Each is covered by a contrast test. The toggles and the popup were checked
in Kagi in both modes; the dropdown hover was only checked live in dark.

## How it is built

The CSS is generated, not hand-written. `build_theme.py` takes a Catppuccin
Kagi theme and rewrites it for Selenized:

- It replaces the palette block in each scope (light `:root`, and the two
  dark scopes) with Selenized values.
- It renames every `var(--old)` reference using a mapping table, and fails
  if a new name would collide with one already declared.
- It appends the overrides above and the licence header.

The input is `custom.css` from jcrabapple's repository:
<https://github.com/jcrabapple/kagi-catppuccin-light-dark>, at commit
`bf8f57941cf9c3c2fa4e41b2123637946bbbe66a`. The output is byte-identical
when regenerated from that commit.

The first version of this theme was converted from an earlier gist of the
same Catppuccin theme. The script still reproduces that version exactly.

To regenerate and test (needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and
Python 3.13 or later):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jcrabapple/kagi-catppuccin-light-dark.git \
  reference/github
git -C reference/github checkout bf8f57941cf9c3c2fa4e41b2123637946bbbe66a
uv run python build_theme.py reference/github/custom.css kagi-selenized.css
uv run pytest
```

`reference/` is git-ignored. The tests that run against a real input are
skipped for any that is missing. They also run against the earlier gist,
<https://repo.jcrabapple.com/jcrabapple/82208449e52b434a8e695c8124fa3f79>
(revision `1ae117e4a5bc74ff7bbbf3496eef80e4dffe312b`), if it is cloned to
`reference/gist`.

## Credits

- [Selenized](https://github.com/jan-warchol/selenized) by Jan Warchoł.
- The Catppuccin theme this was converted from, by jcrabapple (linked above).
  The gist does not state a licence that I could find, so check with its
  author before redistributing anything derived from it.

## Licence

[MIT No Attribution](LICENSE). The same text is at the top of the CSS file.

**The adaptation was small.** The converter already ran on the new file unchanged: same scopes, same three palette blocks, and no name collisions. I made three changes:
- **New colour literal:** upstream added `circle.clock { fill: rgb(150, 120, 120) }`, a hard-coded muted rose that would have stayed Catppuccin-tinted. It now maps to `var(--dim)`.
- **Trailing newline:** the new file ends with a newline and the old one didn't, which produced a double blank line before my appended rules. I tidied that, and the old gist's output is unaffected.

- **`@media` fix:** upstream fixed the unclosed `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block, so the shared rules now apply in light mode as well as dark. Light mode may look slightly different.
- **My overrides:** upstream has no rules for the filter dropdown, the domain popup or the `.ranking-note`, and its toggle rules use the same selectors as before. My appended overrides come later in the file, so they should still win.
- **File size:** the generated CSS differs from the committed one by about 450 lines, mostly upstream's reorganisation and comments.

- **Not applied to Kagi.** Your live theme is still the previous CSS. I didn't paste the new one, since it changes how your light mode looks. If you want, I can apply it and check light and dark, including whether my overrides still win.
